# Results — Study 786 (Flu-Season)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**the pharmacy tape (CVS) rallies into flu season**: bid up ahead of the CDC-defined
October flu-season start. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month). Fingerprint `804082b9d653` (CVS + SPY, one combined panel,
adjusted/total-return daily closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, `CVS` (CVS Health) + `SPY` (S&P 500), one combined panel: 5,154 rows, 2006-01-03 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 19 flu-season starts 2007→2025, each anchored on the fixed CDC **October-1** season start (MMWR week-40 convention; no year-to-year slippage) |
| Events resolvable | all **19** of 19 seasons have CVS+SPY coverage around the anchor |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the abnormal return (CVS − SPY) across independent, non-overlapping yearly events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per cut; leave-one-out jackknife |
| Execution / costs | **calendar-known, zero look-ahead**: the October-1 season start is a fixed convention. Run-up = [anchor−K → anchor]; in-season = [anchor → anchor+K]; net of 2× one-way cost × NAV. Gross AND net reported |
| Price basis | **total-return** (dividends reinvested, `auto_adjust=True`) for both legs |

**Beta, named:** CVS is a defensive healthcare/retail name with a below-market beta
(~0.6-0.8), so a raw `CVS − SPY` difference over a drifting window is partly mechanical.
The run-up/in-season windows here are short (2-4 weeks), so beta is a minor contaminant —
but it is the reason we quote the *abnormal* return throughout, never the raw CVS move.

## The run-up — abnormal return, K sessions BEFORE the season start (CVS − SPY)

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up (k=10) | 19 | −0.078% | −0.109 | 9/19 = 47.4% [27.3%, 68.3%] |
| 1-month run-up (k=21) | 19 | +1.124% | +1.018 | 11/19 = 57.9% [36.3%, 76.9%] |

The bullish folklore is **absent**. The 2-week run-up is essentially zero (−0.08%,
*t* = −0.11); the 1-month run-up is mildly positive (+1.12%) but statistically
indistinguishable from noise (*t* = +1.02) and swamped by CVS's ordinary tracking error.
There is no reliable "rally into flu season."

## The in-season leg — abnormal return, K sessions AFTER the season start

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week in-season (k=10) | 19 | −0.231% | −0.225 | 10/19 = 52.6% [31.7%, 72.7%] |
| 1-month in-season (k=21) | 19 | −1.402% | −0.909 | 8/19 = 42.1% [23.1%, 63.7%] |

The in-season leg is also a clean zero — both cuts |*t*| < 1. If anything CVS drifts
slightly *down* relative to SPY once the season is underway, but nowhere near
significantly.

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per event)

| cut | tail | observed | placebo mean (sd) | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up | right | −0.078% | +0.003% (1.078%) | 0.530 |
| 2-week in-season | left | −0.231% | +0.003% (1.078%) | 0.412 |

Both observed means sit **dead-centre** of the luck cloud (p ≈ 0.53 and 0.41) — exactly
what you expect when there is no effect: the season windows look like any other random
2-week window on CVS vs SPY.

## Jackknife (leave-one-out) — 2-week run-up *t*

Full-sample *t* = **−0.109**; across all 19 leave-one-out draws the *t* stays in
**[−0.529, +0.310]** — it never approaches significance in either direction, so there is
no hidden single-year effect being averaged away either.

## Tradability — net of costs (calendar-known entry, zero look-ahead)

| window | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up | −0.078% (*t* −0.11) | −0.178% (*t* −0.25) | −0.278% (*t* −0.39) |
| 2-week in-season | −0.231% (*t* −0.22) | −0.331% (*t* −0.32) | −0.431% (*t* −0.42) |

Nothing to bank: the gross edge is already indistinguishable from zero, and costs only
push it negative. There is no side of this trade with a real edge.

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (bump = 0), 20 seeds:** mean *t* = +0.28 (sd 0.91); |*t*| ≥ 2 in **0/20** seeds —
  the detector is quiet on the null at n = 19 events with a 10-day AR.
- **Planted run-up +1.0% (seed 813):** mean AR +0.21%, *t* = +0.20.
- **Planted run-up +2.0% (seed 813):** mean AR +1.21%, *t* = **+1.15** — the planted bump
  is recovered monotonically (a +3.0% plant lifts *t* past ~2.1), confirming the machinery
  would fire on a real pre-season rally if one existed. It doesn't.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the effect real?** | **None** | Every cut is indistinguishable from noise: 2-week run-up −0.08% (*t* = −0.11), 1-month run-up +1.12% (*t* = +1.02), in-season legs both |*t*| < 1, placebo p ≈ 0.53/0.41 (dead-centre), jackknife *t* never leaves [−0.53, +0.31]. The synthetic control confirms the detector *would* fire on a real ~3% pre-season rally — there simply isn't one. |
| **Tradability — survives costs/scale?** | **Mirage** | Nothing to bank. The gross edge is ~zero on every window and costs only make it worse; there is no positive-expectancy side to trade. |

**In one sentence:** the "buy the drugstores into flu season" folklore does not survive
contact with the tape — CVS's abnormal return into and through the CDC-defined October
flu-season start is statistically indistinguishable from any random two-week window, in
every specification.
